Britain's Best Viewpoints: Where to Stop and Stare

Part of the joy of motorcycle touring is stopping to take in the views. Britain has an extraordinary number of spectacular viewpoints accessible directly from the road — many with parking suitable for motorcycles. Here are our twenty favourites, from Highland summits to English clifftops.

Scotland

  • 1. Bealach na Bà Summit — Views across the Inner Sound to Skye and the Outer Hebrides. Britain's most dramatic road viewpoint
  • 2. Rest and Be Thankful (A83) — Classic Highland viewpoint looking down Glen Croe. Pull into the old military road for the best views
  • 3. Quiraing, Skye — Otherworldly landscape of pinnacles and plateaux. Small car park at the road summit
  • 4. Kylesku Bridge Viewpoint — Stunning view of the curved bridge spanning the sea loch. NC500 highlight
  • 5. Commando Memorial, Spean Bridge — Views across the Great Glen to Ben Nevis. Moving memorial to WWII commandos

Northern England

  • 6. Hartside Summit (A686) — 580 metres with panoramic views across the Eden Valley to the Lake District
  • 7. Honister Pass Summit — Views down into both Buttermere and Borrowdale. Slate mine car park
  • 8. Buttertubs Pass Summit — Yorkshire Dales panorama across Swaledale and Wensleydale
  • 9. Carter Bar (A68) — Scottish-English border viewpoint with panoramic views both ways
  • 10. Dunstanburgh Castle — Dramatic cliff-top castle ruins on the Northumberland coast

Wales

  • 11. Black Mountain Road Summit (A4069) — Views across the Towy Valley from the Brecon Beacons
  • 12. Pen-y-Pass, Snowdonia — Views of Snowdon, Crib Goch, and the Llanberis Pass
  • 13. Great Orme, Llandudno — Marine Drive road around the headland with views across Conwy Bay
  • 14. Mwnt, Ceredigion — Tiny church on a clifftop overlooking Cardigan Bay, dolphins in summer
The best viewpoints are often unmarked. Keep your eyes open for layby pull-ins on mountain roads — many offer views that rival the official viewpoints without the crowds.

Southern England

  • 15. Beachy Head, Sussex — 162-metre chalk cliffs above the Channel, England's highest sea cliff
  • 16. Durdle Door Viewpoint, Dorset — The iconic limestone arch, short walk from the car park
  • 17. Porlock Hill, Somerset — Looking down onto Porlock Bay and across the Bristol Channel to Wales
  • 18. Symonds Yat Rock, Wye Valley — Viewpoint over the meandering River Wye, peregrine falcons nesting on the cliff
  • 19. Broadway Tower, Cotswolds — 18th-century folly with views across 16 counties on clear days
  • 20. Mam Tor, Peak District — The Shivering Mountain, with views across the Hope Valley

Photography Tips

The best light for photography at UK viewpoints is early morning and late evening — the golden hour transforms British landscapes. Scottish viewpoints are at their best in the long summer evenings. Carry a microfibre cloth for your camera lens — salt spray, mist, and rain are constant companions at British viewpoints.
keyTakeaways: The Bealach na Ba summit on Skye's doorstep is Britain's most dramatic road viewpoint, looking across the Inner Sound to the Hebrides.
Many of the finest viewpoints double as classic road summits, including Hartside (580m), Honister Pass and Buttertubs Pass in northern England.
Southern England offers spectacular coastal stops such as Beachy Head, Durdle Door and Porlock Hill overlooking the Bristol Channel.
The best light for photography is the golden hour at early morning and late evening, and Scottish viewpoints excel in long summer evenings.
Keep watching for unmarked laybys on mountain roads, which often rival the official viewpoints without the crowds.

faq.q: Which is the best road viewpoint in Britain?
faq.a: The summit of the Bealach na Ba in Wester Ross is widely regarded as Britain's most dramatic road viewpoint, with views across the Inner Sound to Skye and the Outer Hebrides. As the reward at the top of Britain's most demanding pass, it combines a thrilling climb with an unforgettable panorama.

faq.q: When is the best time of day to photograph UK viewpoints?
faq.a: The golden hour of early morning and late evening gives the best light, transforming British landscapes with warm tones and long shadows. Scottish viewpoints are especially rewarding in the long summer evenings. Carry a microfibre cloth for your lens, as salt spray, mist and rain are constant companions at exposed British viewpoints.

faq.q: Are these viewpoints accessible directly from the road?
faq.a: Most are accessible directly from the road or a short walk away, many with parking suitable for motorcycles. Road summit viewpoints like Hartside, Honister Pass and Buttertubs Pass require no walking at all, while coastal stops such as Durdle Door involve a short stroll from the car park.

faq.q: Where are the best coastal viewpoints in southern England?
faq.a: Beachy Head in Sussex offers 162-metre chalk cliffs above the Channel, England's highest sea cliff. Durdle Door in Dorset frames the iconic limestone arch a short walk from parking, and Porlock Hill in Somerset looks down onto Porlock Bay and across the Bristol Channel to Wales.

faq.q: How do I find the best unofficial viewpoints?
faq.a: Keep your eyes open for layby pull-ins on mountain roads. Many offer views that rival the official viewpoints without the crowds. Roads like the A83 at the Rest and Be Thankful have several informal stopping points, and the old military road there gives one of the finest Highland outlooks.
